title: Allow Reading and Writing XSF with origin and span_vec
body:
This proposes to read more values from XCrysden files, namely the origin of the values and the size of the box in which data is present (`span_vec`).
Also gives the option to write this information to XSF files, if known.
author: bremerle

comments.author: bremerle
comments.body:
Did not yet remove this, but from my understanding it behaves like follows:
This "strange" division builds a box around the atoms given in the XSF file. `(shape[i] + 1) / shape[i]` scales it to be larger than the dimensions of the molecule. This scaling gets smaller the more data points are written on an axis - 5 data points make the spanning vector 20% larger than the molecules bounding box, but with 100 points it's just 1%. Regardless, the molecule always will be located inside the spanning vector. TBH, looks like a hack to me, to have sensible values here, because none can be provided to the write method itself.

With Octopus on the other hand, a certain volume is simulated. This volume can hand a user defined shape and size, therefore the spanning vector written by Octopus can have arbitrary values. From the XSF documentation I could not see there are any limitations or rules for these values.
